_comment: The loop each invented user ran, the rules that keep a run honest, the interview and the record format. Adapted from newsroom.sgit.ai's how-to (https://newsroom.sgit.ai/articles/how-to-run-synthetic-users.html), with the changes listed in adapted.
loop: observe: a screenshot at the persona's own window size
say what you see, at the detail this persona takes in
think: what they weigh, what they suspect
question: one the page raised and did not answer
confusion: if any, pointing at something on the screenshot
act: one action, with the reason in the persona's terms
loop, until they get what they came for, leave, or run out of patience
rules: stay in the persona; never claim to be a real person
never use knowledge the persona would not have; a page not opened is a page not known
leaving is a valid ending, and often the most useful one
do not fix the site in the narration; that belongs in the interview
every confusion points at something on the screenshot
decide each action from the screenshot alone: never the HTML, the DOM or the markdown twin
browser: feedback/synthetic/tools/step.mjs and driver.mjs: one browser per run that stays open, so the meter's session and the scroll position are those of a real tab. It reaches only a local copy of the site, by GET, and the two pinned APIs the site loads code from; every other request is refused and written in _capture.json.
interview: In one sentence, what is this site?
Was any of it for you? Which part?
Did you believe it? What made you believe it, or not?
Where did you have to guess?
What did you still not know at the end?
Was the credit and the price of each page right for what you got?
Would you install a behaviour policy from here, today? If not, what would have to change?
Would you send this to somebody else? Who?
Rate the experience from 1 to 5, and say why in one sentence.
record: run.json: persona, ended (got-it, left, patience, cap), steps [{n, shot, saw, thought, question, confusion, action, why}], interview [{q, a}], rating, findings [{title, page, step, costs, detail}]
adapted: question 6 asks about the credit and page prices, not a purchase
question 7 asks about installing, the site's one action
the costs name this site's outcomes: the first install, trust, a customer
the browser stays open for the whole run, the first change the newsroom study asked for
